Riftbound x T1 2025 Worlds Champion Collection (setCode T1S, printed bottom-left as "T1S · NNN/005 · EN"). Riot distributes this collection by Riot Merch Store DRAWING, not through retail, so it will never appear in RiftScribe, TCGplayer's catalogue or the riftbound.gg sitemap the automated pipelines read — this file is the only way these six printings exist on RiftCompare at all. Card data was read off Riot's own reveal renders (re-hosted at public/t1-worlds-cards/, cropped out of the composite on the reveal page — same self-host approach as the Vendetta Signature block above, never a hotlink). CROSS-CHECKED, not guessed: Xin Zhao/Galio/Miss Fortune already exist in our DB as base printings (SFD 176, UNL 171, OGN 193) and their domain/type/cost/might match these renders exactly, and Ambessa, The Wolf matches VEN 084 (Body, Unit, 4 energy, 4 might, identical Empower text). Seraphine, Not Alone has no other printing — it is from the unreleased Radiance set and is NOT tournament-legal until Radiance ships — so its Order domain is read from the yellow domain bar, the same colour as the two DB-confirmed Order cards in this same frame. rarity is Showcase for all six per constants.ts chasePrintRarity(): every card here is a special treatment (new art, new frame, new foiling) of another card, so it belongs in Showcase rather than cluttering the base tier its retail printing sits in. NO SETS ENTRY on purpose — T1S is a sealed collector product, not a playable set, and adding it to constants.ts SETS would push a 5-card 'set' into pack-sim, box-EV, movers and the homepage set grid. These cards carry no store listings (they cannot be bought as singles), so card-price-state.ts noindexes their pages until secondary-market listings appear — which is correct and self-healing. Run: `npm run cards:manual` (or maintenance.yml task=cards-manual). isPromo IS TRUE on all six, deliberately: they are a promotional printing in the sense the site's own filters mean it — never sold as a retail single, only handed out through a Riot promotion — so /browse?promo=1 finds them and each tile carries the PROMO badge. TWO CONSEQUENCES worth knowing. (1) cardSlug() appends "-promo", so the URLs are /card/<name>-t1s-<num>-005-promo; both T1 articles' embed slug lists were updated to match and tests/content-links.test.ts covers the articles' internal links. (2) chasePrintRarity() leaves a promo's rarity alone rather than forcing Showcase, which is why rarity is set explicitly to Showcase in each entry above instead of being inferred.

_note: KOREAN EVENT PROMOS (added 2026-09-11). Riftbound's first Korean-market promos, both handed out in person at the MSI Fan Festa in Daejeon, 3-12 July 2026, ahead of Origins' Korean release on 18 September. Numbers taken from the printed cards and cross-checked against live sale listings: Jinx is 'OGN 030/298 P KR' and Yasuo is 'OGN 076b/298 P KR'. GAME DATA IS THE BASE CARD'S, because a promo printing is the same card: Jinx, Demolitionist is Fury 3/4 and Yasuo, Remorseful is Calm 6/6, both read from prisma/riftbound-cards.json rather than typed from memory. NAMES ARE DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED — no '(Korean)' suffix. The card page groups printings with `where: { name: card.name }`, so a renamed promo would vanish from 'Other printings' on the base card, which is the single best way anyone actually finds one of these. The trade-off is that a site search for 'korean yasuo' will not match on name; the PROMO badge and collector number carry the distinction on the page. NO IMAGE, on purpose. dotgg has no scan for either number (both 404), and the only art available is on a competing retailer's own blog CDN — not ours to republish, and it would break the moment they reorganise. Borrowing the base card's art is worse than a placeholder and is a mistake this file has already made once: see the 197b/151b note above, where promos silently inherited the base face and showed the wrong card. Same reason scripts/fix-cloned-art.ts exists. Fill these in when a real scan appears. THEY WILL NEVER SHOW A PRICE, and that is by design rather than a gap: FOREIGN_LANG in lib/scrape-http.ts matches both the Hangul range and a bare 'kr'/'kor', and every price source checks it FIRST — resolveCardId returns null, isNonEnglishProduct drops the product at the top of the loop before byExternal is even consulted (so a PROMO_PRODUCT_OVERRIDES pin cannot reach them either), and eBay filters the same way. That guard is what stops a Chinese print stealing an English card's price, so it is not being loosened for two cards. Pricing these would need a deliberate per-card 'this card IS the foreign printing' exemption, which is its own decision.

RADIANCE SPOILER, added 2026-09-19 from a photograph of the physical card. This is the FIRST Radiance card in the catalogue, so it is also the first hard evidence of the set's printed denominator: the card reads 'RAD - 167/167 - EN', which is why setFromTotal() in lib/price-import.ts now maps 167 to RAD and no longer guesses 114/180, and why constants.ts SETS carries totalCards 167 rather than Riot's announced 180. EVERY FIELD IS READ OFF THE CARD except rarity, which was VERIFIED rather than guessed: the bottom-centre rarity gem is an orange pentagon, matched pixel-for-pixel against Sett, Brawler (OGN-164, epic) and against Kayn, Unleashed (OGN-189, rare, a magenta diamond) pulled from cdn.riftscribe.gg. Domain is 'Colorless' — the card's own wording is 'Neutral', but Colorless is the value all 65 existing neutral rows use and what lib/domains.ts, the facet pages and the /browse filters are built on; inventing a second spelling would orphan the card from every one of them. Type tags read 'CHAMPION UNIT - NEEKO - IXTAL'. Artist credit on the card is Luscinia Studio, (c)2026 RGI. REPLACE imageUrl with the RiftScribe CDN art the moment the automated import carries this card — the photo is a stopgap, and `npm run cards:sync` will not overwrite a manual row.

_note: RADIANCE PREVIEW-SEASON REVEALS, added 2026-09-29 from the card images StarCityGames gathered in 'Every Card Revealed So Far From Riftbound: Radiance' (articles.starcitygames.com, 29 Sept) — a round-up of the first days of Preview Season, 25 Sept onward. 24 new rows: 20 base-run cards (among them K'Sante, Courageous' first base printing) and four chase printings. EVERY FIELD IS READ OFF THE CARD IMAGES: name and epithet, the type line (a 'CHAMPION UNIT' is type Unit, a 'SIGNATURE SPELL' is type Spell, as elsewhere in this file), energy (top left), Might (top right), the rules text, and the collector number printed bottom left. RARITY is the bottom-centre gem, each one zoomed and matched against cdn.riftscribe.gg reference crops (white circle Common, teal triangle Uncommon, magenta diamond Rare, orange pentagon Epic, gold Showcase), never inferred from the card's power level. DOMAIN is the domain gem; the three two-domain Legends are filed under the FIRST (top) gem, the same one-domain convention as the Seraphine and K'Sante Legends above: Ekko Fury (over Mind), Ziggs Fury (over Chaos), Orianna Calm (over Mind); Hexplosive Minefield carries Ziggs' pair and is filed Fury with him. Rakelstake is a Battlefield, so Colorless like all 56 catalogued battlefields; its image was rotated to landscape. TEXT STYLE follows the HEARTSTEEL rows: keywords in brackets, printed reminder text left off, one ability per line, the any-rune symbol as [A] and exhaust as [Exhaust]. CHASE PRINTINGS: 090a/167 is Evelynn, Consuming's alternate art (artist credit 黯荧岛 Dark Glow), and 169*/167, 171*/167 and 174*/167 are Signature prints (Ziggs by Kindlejack, Orianna by Anh Dang, Seraphine by Anna Nikonova), all with the gold Showcase gem. SERAPHINE 174 vs 174*: the image shows '174*/167' with the artist's signature across the art. The existing 174/167 row above is NOT renumbered: in every earlier set a Signature Legend came in a pair, an unsigned over-numbered printing and a signed twin with the same number plus '*' (OGN 303/298 + 303*/298, SFD 224/221 + 224*/221, VEN 190/166 + 190*/166), and 174/167 is the printing Riot's 24 Sept reveal named. So 174*/167 is its own row, and 174/167 keeps no image rather than borrowing the signed art. By the same pattern Ziggs 169/167 and Orianna 171/167 probably exist unsigned; they are NOT added until one is seen. NOT ADDED, on purpose: Ahri, Confident, Invigorating Bloom and Supernova (059/167) appear in the round-up, but in each the collector number or the rarity gem is cropped or smeared, and this file does not take half-read cards; the Bomb and Mech tokens (the catalogue carries no tokens); Sett, Kingpin OGN 240 (an Origins card, shown for comparison). NAME SHARING: K'Sante, Courageous now has a base (086) and a HEARTSTEEL (178) printing, Seraphine, Not Alone a RAD 138 and a T1S printing, and Evelynn, Orianna and Ziggs each a base and a chase print. tests/radiance-preview-matching.test.ts pins that a bare-name store listing resolves to the base printing and a numbered or 'Signature'/'Alternate Art' listing to the chase print. IMAGES are self-hosted crops of the round-up's card renders (public/radiance-spoilers/); REPLACE them with the official art once Riot's gallery carries these cards — `npm run cards:sync` never overwrites a manual row. (SUPERSEDED 2026-09-30 on Seraphine 174: Riot's gallery shows only the signed 174*/167, so the unsigned 174/167 row is retired — see the official-gallery note below.)

_note: RADIANCE — EVERY CARD IN RIOT'S OFFICIAL GALLERY, 2026-09-30. At the owner's instruction ('use anything Riot as a source of truth'), the Radiance catalogue now matches playriftbound.com's card gallery, all 84 printings: 37 added here, and the 47 already in this file brought into line. WHAT COMES FROM WHERE, all of it Riot: the card image (the gallery's cmsassets.rgpub.io asset, used as imageUrl on every Radiance row, so the self-hosted crops in public/radiance-spoilers are no longer the card art), the rules text (the gallery's own rich text, converted to the catalogue's token format — [S] Might, [T] exhaust, [N] energy, [A] any rune, [C] a domain rune — and identical, card for card, to the gallery's accessibility text, which is what the automated importer stores for every other set), the name and collector number, and the rarity (it matches the printed gem on every card). Domain, type, Energy and Might are READ OFF THE PRINTED CARD, because the gallery's metadata fields disagree with Riot's own card images on those for many Radiance cards (e.g. Amateur Demolitionist, Bilgewater Tracker and Runeblade Anvil filed Chaos/Body/Chaos but printed with the Fury icon; Supernova filed an Order Unit, printed a Mind SPELL; Runeblade Anvil filed a Unit, printed GEAR; Command: Attack filed a Gear, printed SPELL). Domain is the printed domain icon bottom right, the first of two for the two-domain cards (Blade of the Exile Calm over Chaos; Exemplar of Demacia Body over Order). Two fixes to Riot's text: Rousing Display's ends 'instead.disa' in the data and 'instead.' on the card; a double space on Ekko's Legend. Blade of the Exile's printed '+3' Might bonus and Ganking line are not in Riot's text data, so they are not in the description either, and no gear carries a Might value in this catalogue. NAMES: Legends are 'Champion, Epithet' like every other Legend here, champion from the gallery's tags — which renames the two Pride of Nazumah rows to 'K'Sante, Pride of Nazumah' so K'Sante's champion page finds them (lib/champions.ts matches the 'K'Sante,' prefix); lib/card-slug-renames.ts moves their URLs. SERAPHINE 174: Riot's gallery lists ONE printing at 174, and its image is the signed art printed '174*/167'. The unsigned 174/167 row, which no Riot source shows, is removed from this file and retired by scripts/add-manual-cards.ts (deleted only if no user alert, holding or listing points at it); its URL redirects to the 174* page. This supersedes the 2026-09-29 note above that kept it as a separate printing. Runes are numbered as Riot prints them (R02, R02A, R03, R03A), like Vendetta's. The SP printings stay isPromo false, as Vendetta's six SP cards are in the live catalogue.
